Q107451258.summary: Ariel Henry is a Haitian neurosurgeon and politician who served as the acting prime minister of Haiti after the assassination of Jovenel Moïse in 2021 until his resignation in 2025.

Q5290874.label: 1995 Dominican general election
Q5290874.summary: General elections were held in Dominica on 12 June 1995. Although the Dominica Freedom Party received the most votes, the United Workers' Party won 11 of the 21 seats. Voter turnout was 65.2%, the lowest since universal suffrage was introduced in 1951.

Q17087354.label: 1935 Salvadoran presidential election
Q17087354.summary: Presidential elections were held in El Salvador between 13 and 15 January 1935. Brigadier General Maximiliano Hernández Martínez was the only candidate and was elected unopposed with 329,555 votes.

Q7129978.label: 1932 Panamanian general election
Q7129978.summary: General elections were held in Panama on 5 June 1932 to elect a new President of the Republic and a new National Assembly. Harmodio Arias Madrid of the Liberal Doctrinaire Party (PLDo) was elected President, whilst the PLDo emerged as the largest party in the National Assembly, winning 14 of the 32 seats.

Q16353146.label: Dritan Abazović
Q16353146.summary: Dritan Abazović is a Montenegrin politician who served as Prime Minister of Montenegro and as acting Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2022 to 2023. An ethnic Albanian, he heads the United Reform Action party. He previously served as deputy prime minister in the cabinet of Zdravko Krivokapić from 2020 until 2022.

Q16970106.label: Slovenian archives law referendum, 2014
Q16970106.summary: A referendum on the archive law was held in Slovenia on 8 June 2014. Voters were asked whether they were in favor of the amendments to the law that were passed in January 2014. The amendments were rejected by 67% of voters, although the referendum was invalidated by "no" voters accounting for only 7.79% of all registered voters, well below the 20% quorum.

Q3788154.label: 1990 Kazakh Supreme Soviet election
Q3788154.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in Kazakhstan on 25 March 1990. Of the 360 seats, 270 were directly elected, whilst 90 were selected by public associations. The Communist Party of Kazakhstan won 342 of the 360 seats, with the remainder going to independents. Voter turnout was reported to be 84%.

Q2052986.label: 2002 Latvian parliamentary election
Q2052986.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Latvia on 5 October 2002. The New Era Party emerged as the largest party in the Saeima, winning 26 of the 100 seats.

Q18071930.label: Siege of Kobanî
Q18071930.desc: 2014 battle in the Syrian Civil War
Q18071930.img: Coalition Airstrike on ISIL position in Kobane.jpg
Q18071930.summary: The siege of Kobanî was launched by the Islamic State (IS) on 13 September 2014, in order to capture the Kobanî Canton and its main city of Kobanî in northern Syria, in the de facto autonomous region of Rojava.

Q689018.label: Socialist Workers' Party of Germany
Q689018.summary: The Socialist Workers' Party of Germany was a centrist Marxist political party in Germany. It was formed as a left-wing party with around 20,000 members who split off from the SPD in the autumn of 1931. In 1931, the remnants of the USPD merged into the party and in 1932 some Communist Party dissenters also joined the group as well as a part of the Communist Party Opposition. Nevertheless, SAPD membership remained small. From 1933, the group's members worked illegally against Nazism.

Q1399162.label: Virtue Party
Q1399162.summary: Virtue Party was an Islamist political party established on 17 December 1997 in Turkey. It was found unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court and then banned on 22 June 2001 for violating the secularist articles of the Constitution. After the party's ban, the party MPs founded two sections of parties: reformist Justice and Development Party (AKP), headed by Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, and traditionalist Felicity Party (SP), headed by Recai Kutan.

Q83834.label: anti-Sovietism
Q83834.desc: opposition to Soviet Union, its government and its policies
Q83834.summary: Anti-Sovietism or anti-Soviet sentiment are activities that were actually or allegedly aimed against the Soviet Union or government power within the Soviet Union.
